transcript.content: Hello. What brings you in to see me today?
I’m here because I’ve been making myself throw up after I eat too much, so I won’t gain weight. It’s… it’s not just happened once. It’s becoming something I keep doing, and that scared me.
Has your weight dropped to a point where doctors or loved ones consider you significantly underweight?
I’m not sure. I haven’t really noticed that anyone thinks I’m significantly underweight.
During those times when you feel you eat too much, do you feel a sense of loss of control, like you can't stop eating or control what you are eating?
Yes. Once I start, it’s like I’m on automatic. I’ll be thinking I should stop before my husband notices, but I still keep reaching for one more thing.
On average, how many times a week does this happen?
Most weeks, at least once a week—for the past several months. It isn’t just occasional anymore.

latest_inference.note: Frequency and duration (at least once weekly for several months) meet the full criteria for bulimia nervosa, ruling out atypical or unspecified eating disorders (F50.8, F50.9).
